findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT- There was salmon in reduced oxygen packaging in the top of the preparation cooler that was observed to still be in its original packaging. The label and packaging states to remove from packaging prior to thawing. Proper thawing procedures were discussed with the staff. Thawing should only be done through refrigeration, the cooking process, or under cold running water to prevent bacteria growth. CORRECTED- All packages of reduced oxygen packaged salmon that were thawed or currently being thawed had their package cut. Ensure that staff are educated on proper thawing procedures. findings.comment:

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The following items were found improperly cold holding above 41F:

Following items noted stored at room temperature on countertop across from cookline: cut tomatoes 49F, large container of spouts 44F-48F, cooked tofu 45F. Items were placed into ice bath at the time of inspection. PIC indicated items are usually used during lunch rush, however leftovers are move back into cold holding. Discussed importance of keeping cold foods below 41F. Discussed using ice baths of obtaining a countertop cold holding unit.

In sliding door cooler on the server side of the pass thru window: (TOP) lettuce/noodle spring rolls 66F,  (BOTTOM) half and half 45F. Ambient temperature of top 50F-51FF, ambient temperature of bottom 45F.  Spring rolls were moved into proper cold holding unit. 

-> Cold held food items must be maintained below 41F for proper food safety. If using ice baths, ensure products are fully submerged in ice. Do not leave food out at room temperature without means of proper cold holding temperatures. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-830 Dishmachine was not leaving a chloring residual during the inspection. Machine was primed and tubes were fiddled with until suction was created. A residual of approx. 100ppm Cl was observed during inspection. The sani-buckets throughout the facility contained soap and no sanitizing residual. Buckets at the dishmachine, wait station, and the cookline all tested 0ppm Cl or Quat. Discussed labeling buckets for soap and water AND sanitizing cloths for food contact surfaces of cookline.  All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) The following food contact surfaces are observed soiled: 1) the canopener is soiled with food debris; and 2) the top of the dishmachine is soiled with mineral accumulation.  To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The following non-food contacts surfaces are observed soiled: 1) fans within the walk-in cooler are moldy; and 2) the white wire shelves around the wait station have rease and dust accumulation.  Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 Backdoor was observed cracked throughout most of the inspection. Door had to be pulled extremely hard to insure tight-fitting. Corrected during inspection. Make sure that door is repaired to insure staff is able to propely close the door. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 The floor infront of the mop sink is broken (cracked tiles). ALSO, the floor drain beneath the prep cooler of the cookline is soiled with mold accumulation. Clean the attached plumbing leading into the drain too.  All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Pork and Beef in the top of the prep cooler are 50F or above. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times. (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) The beef and pork were discarded.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: Dish machine is not showing any chlorine residual. 750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration. Dish machine is now reading at 50ppm of chlorine. The repair tech was here and fixed the machine.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: The spoons at the wait area are stored with handles and eating ends mixed. Also some plates are stored with the eating surfaces exposed. 750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.
